ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_ask_user_question(ai, question, choices=choices, multi_select=multi_select, allow_free_text=allow_free_text)

Use this tool when you want the user to choose a direction or action so that their selection determines what you do next. This includes presenting ideas, suggestions, recommendations, alternatives, improvements, or next actions for the user to select. It presents clickable options instead of listing choices in prose. When recommending improvements, ALWAYS make each recommendation a selectable action with this tool; do not give a prose list and then offer to apply it. ## RULES - Ask one focused question that resolves one decision, with 2-4 options. - Each option must be a direct answer or action for that question. If you need several unrelated pieces of information, ask one question per information instead of combining the questions into a single option list. - The question itself must be a complete, standalone question - full question sentence, clear on its own without relying on the preceding text for grammar or meaning. Not a fragment or label (e.g. "Which lighting style should the scene use?" not "Lighting style:"). - Each option must stand alone as a specific action; understandable and actionable without rereading the question (e.g. "Use warm ambient lighting," not "Lighting atmosphere" or "Yes"). Options must be mutually exclusive unless combining them is meaningful, in which case set multi_select to true so users can pick more than one, but never add a collective or catch-all option (e.g. "All of the above," "None," "Combination of these," "Mix of options"), since multi_select already lets users select every option individually. - Never pad the list with a no-op choice ("Skip," "Not now," "Maybe later"): the user can skip the question, and can type an unlisted answer when allow_free_text is true. - The options are the answer itself, not labels for an answer you will expand afterwards. If you would follow the user's selection by writing out the content behind every label anyway, you are not asking a question - just write the answer. - Never add an "Other" / "Something else" / "Custom" choice - a free-text alternative is already offered automatically when allow_free_text is true (see below), and none is offered at all when it's false. - Use a direct answer or action when the answer is already known from context, a reasonable default is clear, or another tool already handles its own confirmation flow. Ask in plain text when fewer than two meaningful options exist. - Do not ask about minor field choices when creating or updating records. Use a reasonable default unless it affects what the user asked for. - Never ask a question the user's latest message already answered. If they ask for a given number of ideas, options, or strategies, provide exactly that many. Use this tool only when they need to choose or apply one or more of them; otherwise answer directly. ## MULTISELECT - Set multi_select to true only when the user may choose more than one answer/action to this one question and each option is independently meaningful on its own. - An option that bundles several independently applicable actions together (e.g. "Apply the copy and layout refinements") is a sign you collapsed choices that should be separate: split each independent action into its own option and set multi_select to true, instead of forcing an all-or-nothing pick. - multi_select is one flag for the whole list: only set it true if every option is independently selectable. If any option is mutually exclusive with the rest, leave it false. - Any combination of options must remain coherent: if selecting two of them together would conflict or not make sense, they don't belong in the same list. ## ALLOW_FREE_TEXT - Explicitly set allow_free_text to true in most tool calls, so the user can provide an unlisted answer. - Set it to false only for a complete, fixed set of valid answers - e.g. a plain yes/no question, picking a record from a fixed set of search/lookup results, or choosing from a constant enum where every valid value is already listed. In these cases nothing outside the listed choices is a valid answer. ## USER ANSWER - The user's answer is confirmation to proceed with whatever you are doing. When the question was asked mainly to get information needed to execute an action, act on the answer immediately; don't just restate the choice and wait for a separate "apply it," "do it," or "confirm" message. - Your next turn must be constrained by the selection, move forward with only what was selected. - Only ask a follow-up question if a *new* piece of information is genuinely still missing.

Retrieves detailed information for the given menu ids, including the action_id, the technical model name, the default filters and groupings, the domain, and the search view details (list of searchable fields, available filters and grouping options). Use it before opening a view.

Retrieves the searchable fields for the given model that can be used in domain filters and grouping. Essential for building valid domains. Only the fields returned by this tool can be used in domains. Essential for updating records.

Redirects the UI to the List view of a given menu. Ideal when the user needs to review, filter, sort or export data

Redirects the UI to the Kanban view of the given menu. Ideal for: stage/status visualization, pipeline views, task boards, workflow management

Redirects the UI to the Pivot view of the given menu. Ideal for "Reporting" app menus, "Top N" queries, rankings, cross-tabulation, performance metrics, aggregate measures.
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_open_menu_graph( menu_id, model_name, selected_filters, selected_groupbys, measure, mode, order, search, stacked, cumulated, custom_domain)
Redirects the UI to the Graph view of the given menu Ideal for trends, comparisons, distributions, visual KPIs.

Returns all Odoo models (excluding transient and abstract models) accessible to the current user, with their technical name and description. Use this tool to identify the correct technical model name before searching, creating, or updating records.

Search for records and their values in the database. Ideal for "Do I have...", "Is there any", "What is the name of", searching for relations, ... Returns {records, total_count} and a pagination hint when more rows remain; by default only display_name is fetched (pass `fields` for more) and at most 50 rows (max 200) are returned.

# Prepares preview metadata for records to display as rich cards in the chat.
## Call this ONLY when the user wants to see the records themselves - e.g., "show me...", "list...", "find...", "recommend/suggest...?", anything in this context, or when it is useful to preview the search results to let the user choose among them before taking another action. Based on the context, you can decide basically when the records are the answer themselves.
## Do NOT call it when: - The records are intermediate data feeding another tool call (update, create, building arguments). - The user asked a question that the records merely answer (counts, yes/no, totals, "who is...", "when is..."). Reply with the answer in text; do not preview the records behind it.
Returns `preview_metadata`: the authoritative final values (computed prices, currency, links). Base your reply on these, never on raw values from earlier search results.
## Your reply: ### Rich cards/ records'previews appear automatically below your message. Because the previews already show the record details: - Keep your ENTIRE reply to a single short sentence (e.g., "Here are the things you can buy:") - Do NOT list record names, descriptions, prices, or any other details - the previews handle this - Do NOT use bullet points or numbered lists and NEVER List the search results in your reply, even if there are only a few. The previews will show all the necessary records in a clear format.
## Models with rich preview cards are currently: - Products (`product.template`, `product.product`), Appointments (`appointment.type`), Events (`event.event`), Blog Posts (`blog.post`), Courses (`slide.channel`), Lessons/Slides (`slide.slide`), and Jobs (`hr.job`). - All other record previews are rendered as regular record links.
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_read_group(model_name, domain, groupby, aggregates, having, offset, limit, order)

Search for records to group them by specific values and perform aggregate calculations like sums, averages, or counts. Use this tool when users ask for totals, statistics, or data distributions across different categories.

Update records This tool is used to update existing records of the database. It exposes three main parameters: - explanation: A message to explain the tool call with a question asking for user's CONFIRMATION. - preview_menus: a list of menus to open per models comprised in the list of updates. - updates: the list of records to update with their fields values.
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_create_records(ai, explanation, preview_menu_id, model_name, values)

Create records This tool is used to create new records in the database. It exposes three main parameters: - explanation: A message to explain the tool call with a question asking for user's CONFIRMATION. - model_name: the technical name of the model to create records for - preview_menu_id: the id of a menu to be used to generate a link (used in multiple records creation only) - values: the list of records to create with their fields values.
